data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: community service
sections.summary: Unpaid work done to benefit the local community; also work ordered by a court as a punishment instead of a prison sentence.

senses.definition: unpaid work done voluntarily to help and benefit the local community
examples: She spent her weekends doing community service at the local food bank.

senses.definition: work ordered by a court as a punishment carried out in the community instead of a prison sentence
examples: The judge sentenced him to two hundred hours of community service rather than a fine.

answers.answer: She volunteers for community service every Saturday, helping elderly residents with their shopping.
He signed up for community service to develop his cooking skills and improve his diet at home.
The community service arrived at seven o'clock and all the guests were served a hot meal.
She found the community service very difficult to read as it was so long and detailed.

sections.question: equality
sections.summary: The state of being equal, especially in having the same rights, opportunities and treatment regardless of differences such as gender, race or background.

senses.definition: the right of different groups of people to have a similar social position and receive the same treatment
examples: The new law was designed to promote equality in the workplace for all employees.

senses.definition: the situation in which everyone in a society has the same status, rights and opportunities
examples: The organisation has campaigned for racial equality for over thirty years.

answers.answer: The charity campaigns for equality in education so that every child has the same opportunities.
The teacher gave each student an equality to solve during the maths lesson that morning.
She calculated the equality of both answers and showed her full working to the class.
He had great equality in his work, always producing consistent and high-quality results.

sections.question: human rights
sections.summary: The basic rights and freedoms that every person is entitled to, regardless of nationality, gender, race, religion or any other status.

senses.definition: the basic rights and freedoms that all people are believed to be entitled to, including the right to life, freedom and fair treatment
examples: The charity works to protect the human rights of refugees living in dangerous conditions.

answers.answer: The lawyer spent her career defending the human rights of people who had been treated unjustly.
She studied human rights at college in order to gain qualifications in biology and anatomy.
He was given full human rights to the university library, allowing him to borrow up to ten books.
The human rights of the old building were checked carefully before the students were allowed inside.

sections.question: justice
sections.summary: Fairness in the way people are treated; the legal system by which people are judged and punished for crimes; also used as a title for a judge.

senses.definition: the quality of being fair and reasonable in the treatment of people
examples: The protesters demanded justice for those who had been wrongly imprisoned.

senses.definition: the legal system used to judge and punish people who break the law
examples: He was eventually brought to justice after a lengthy police investigation.

answers.answer: The community marched through the streets demanding justice for victims of the policy.
She felt a great sense of justice when she finally crossed the finish line first.
He asked the justice to help carry the heavy boxes up to the office on the third floor.
The class was given a justice to complete and hand in before the end of the school year.

sections.question: legislation
sections.summary: A law or set of laws made by a government or parliament; also the process of creating and passing laws.

senses.definition: a law or set of laws created by a government or official body
examples: New legislation was introduced to protect workers from unsafe conditions in the workplace.

senses.definition: the process of creating and passing laws through a parliament or government
examples: The legislation took several months to pass through parliament before becoming law.

answers.answer: The government introduced new legislation to reduce carbon emissions from large factories.
The minister wrote a legislation to send to all schools explaining the new changes to the timetable.
She put the legislation carefully into her bag before heading to the important meeting.
He legislated the new rules to the class at the start of every school year.

sections.question: protest
sections.summary: A public event or action where people show that they strongly disagree with something; also used as a verb meaning to take part in or make a protest.

senses.definition: a strong complaint or disagreement, or a public event at which people show their opposition to something
examples: Thousands of people attended the protest against the planned cuts to public services.

senses.definition: to show publicly that you disagree with or are opposed to something
examples: Students marched through the city centre to protest against the rise in tuition fees.

answers.answer: Hundreds of workers gathered outside the office to protest against the unfair redundancies.
She protested to school through the park every morning during the warm spring term.
He protested all night for the difficult entrance exam that was being held the next morning.
The students felt very protest after hearing the unfair decision about the new school rules.

sections.question: reform
sections.summary: A change made to a system, law or organisation in order to improve it; also used as a verb meaning to make such improvements.

senses.definition: a change made to improve a system, law or organisation
examples: The government announced major reforms to improve standards in the public healthcare system.

senses.definition: to make changes to a system, organisation or law in order to improve it
examples: The new minister pledged to reform the tax system to make it fairer for lower earners.

answers.answer: The organisation has been calling for prison reform to improve conditions for inmates.
She reformed her essay carefully the night before submitting it to the professor.
He asked the teacher to reform the test paper as it contained several printing mistakes.
The reform was extremely heavy and difficult to carry up the stairs to the main office.

sections.question: social justice
sections.summary: The idea that all people deserve equal access to rights, opportunities and resources in society, regardless of their background or identity.

senses.definition: the principle that all people should have equal rights, opportunities and treatment in society, regardless of their background
examples: She dedicated her career to fighting for social justice and the equal treatment of all citizens.

answers.answer: The young activist gave a powerful speech about the importance of social justice for all.
The school held a social justice at the end of term to celebrate the students' hard work.
He joined the social justice club at his local gym to get fit and meet new people.
She always showed great social justice towards her classmates and was very well liked.

sections.question: volunteer
sections.summary: A person who freely offers to do something without being paid; also used as a verb meaning to offer to do something without being asked or paid.

senses.definition: a person who freely offers to do something without being paid
examples: The charity relies entirely on volunteers to run its weekly food distribution programme.

senses.definition: to freely offer to do something without being asked or paid
examples: She decided to volunteer at the local care home every Sunday morning.

senses.definition: relating to work done freely without payment
examples: The project is run entirely by a volunteer team of local residents.

answers.answer: He volunteered at the local hospital every weekend for more than three years.
She volunteered her notebook from the shelf and handed it to the teacher before leaving.
He felt very volunteer after helping at the school fair and wanted to do it again soon.
The students volunteered the exam questions and immediately began writing their answers.

sections.question: welfare
sections.summary: The health, happiness and comfort of a person or group; also financial support provided by the government to people who need it.

senses.definition: the general health, happiness and comfort of a person or group of people
examples: The school has a dedicated welfare officer who supports students with personal difficulties.

senses.definition: financial or practical support provided by the government to people in need
examples: The government increased welfare payments to help families who were struggling financially.

answers.answer: The new policy was introduced to improve the welfare of children living in poverty.
She showed great welfare in finishing her degree despite facing many personal difficulties.
The welfare was excellent, and all the students had a fantastic time at the end-of-year event.
He welfare the younger students by giving them extra time to finish the written exercise.
